outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no event gives a combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients for all triples of partitions. The window holds restricted or partial results: a positive counting rule for two-row first partition with two rectangular partitions (Pak, Panova and Swanson, 4 Nov 2025); a framework giving interpretations for two-row plus hook-like shapes (Campbell, 25 Apr 2026); a conjectured candidate for the general case with only partial results (Harman and Wilson, 18 Jul 2025); a three-row closed-form claim that its author withdrew (Lee, 28 Nov 2025, withdrawn 20 Dec 2025); a computable but non-positive formula for all coefficients (Vallejo and Sanchez Salazar, 18 Oct 2025); and a closed formula for a different species-basis quantity whose title calls it a Kronecker formula (Baolahy and Randrianirina, 4 Sep 2026). Stanley's Problem 10 is still described as open in all sources read.
problem_asks: The statement asks for a combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients g(lambda, mu, nu), where lambda, mu, nu are partitions of n and g(lambda, mu, nu) is the multiplicity of the irreducible S_n character indexed by nu in the tensor product of the irreducibles indexed by lambda and mu. Parts: (1) the quantifier runs over every triple of partitions of every n, not a family or a fixed shape; (2) for each triple, a combinatorial interpretation means a combinatorial family of objects whose count equals g(lambda, mu, nu). The bullet itself does not say 'positive' or 'nonnegative'. The standard reading in the literature (Stanley's Problem 10, which asks for a nonnegative or manifestly positive interpretation; and the Wikipedia article's own description, 'a combinatorial description') treats the wanted object as a counting rule. A rule covering only some shapes (two-row, hook, rectangular, three-row) is a restricted case of part (1), not the whole of it.

events.what_happened: Jonah Blasiak, 'Kronecker coefficients for one hook shape', arXiv:1209.2018 (Sept 2012); published Seminaire Lotharingien de Combinatoire B77c (2017). Gives a positive combinatorial rule for g(lambda, mu(d), nu) when one of the three partitions is a hook mu(d) = (n-d, 1^d) and the other two are arbitrary, counting colored Yamanouchi tableaux built with Haiman's mixed insertion.
events.revisions: v1 Sept 2012 per arXiv id; later versions not checked; journal version SLC B77c (2017).
events.delivers: A positive counting formula for Kronecker coefficients in which one of the three partitions is a hook (any n, any lambda and nu). It is an interpretation for a restricted family of triples.
events.remains: Every triple in which no partition is a hook; the general interpretation asked for in the bullet.
events.direction: Gives a positive interpretation, which is the kind of object the problem asks for, but only for triples with a hook.

events.what_happened: Cristina Ballantine and Rosa Orellana, 'Multiplicities in the Kronecker product s(n-p,p) * s_lambda', arXiv:math/0507544 (submitted 26 July 2005; later retitled 'A Combinatorial Interpretation for the coefficients in the Kronecker Product s(n-p,p) * s_lambda'). Gives a combinatorial interpretation (Kronecker tableaux) for the coefficient of s_nu in s(n-p,p) * s_lambda when lambda is not inside a 2(p-1) x 2(p-1) square; inside the square the rule gives only an upper bound. A narrower companion appeared in Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 12 (2005) R28, and in Seminaire Lotharingien B54Af (2006).
events.revisions: v1 26 July 2005 (title Multiplicities in the Kronecker Product); v2 revised 2013 under the combinatorial-interpretation title (per arXiv listing excerpt).
events.delivers: A combinatorial interpretation for Kronecker coefficients whose first partition has two parts, for lambda outside the 2(p-1) square. It is restricted to two-row first partitions and to lambda outside a square.
events.remains: Two-row first partitions with lambda inside the square (only an upper bound); all other triples.

checked_by.who: Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (refereed journal), for the narrower companion R28; Seminaire Lotharingien de Combinatoire B54Af (2006)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published companion versions of the result

events.direction: Gives a positive-type rule for a restricted family (two-row first partition), with an upper bound elsewhere.

events.what_happened: Christian Ikenmeyer, Ketan Mulmuley and Michael Walter, 'On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients', arXiv:1507.02955 (first version July 2015, revised July 2017; published Computational Complexity 2017). Proves that deciding whether a Kronecker coefficient is positive is NP-hard, so Kronecker coefficients are harder than Littlewood-Richardson coefficients unless P = NP.
events.revisions: v1 July 2015; revised July 2017 (per arXiv listing excerpt).
events.delivers: A complexity result (NP-hardness of deciding positivity) with no interpretation of the coefficients. It bears on how hard an interpretation could be.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the revised version, DOI 10.1007/s00037-017-0158-y (per search excerpt)

events.direction: Does not interpret the coefficients. It shows positivity is hard to decide, which is evidence about how hard an interpretation is. Cuts neither way on the bullet directly.

events.what_happened: Marni Mishna and Stefan Trandafir, 'Estimating and computing Kronecker coefficients: a vector partition function approach', arXiv:2210.12128 (Oct 2022); published Australasian Journal of Combinatorics 90(2), pp. 121-154. Builds on Mishna, Rosas and Sundaram (arXiv:1811.10015), which writes Kronecker coefficients as a signed sum of vector partition function values. They give evaluation, bound and vanishing formulas, including for l(mu) <= 2, l(nu) <= 4, l(lambda) <= 8.
events.revisions: Not checked beyond the journal listing; journal year not confirmed.
events.delivers: Signed-sum (alternating) formulas and bounds for Kronecker coefficients in terms of vector partition functions, for bounded lengths. Not a positive or manifestly combinatorial interpretation.
events.remains: A positive or manifestly combinatorial interpretation for all triples.
events.direction: An alternating-sum formula, not a positive interpretation. Cuts against manifest positivity being reached this way.

events.what_happened: Christian Ikenmeyer and Greta Panova, 'All Kronecker coefficients are reduced Kronecker coefficients', arXiv:2305.03003 (submitted 4 May 2023); Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024) e22; short version in FPSAC 2024 proceedings (SLC 91B.49). Shows each Kronecker coefficient of S_n equals an explicit reduced Kronecker coefficient of slightly larger partitions. Consequence: Stanley's Problem 10 (interpret Kronecker coefficients) and Kirillov's Problem 2.32 (interpret reduced Kronecker coefficients) are equivalent. Also: positivity of reduced coefficients is NP-hard and computing them is #P-hard under parsimonious reductions.
events.revisions: v1 4 May 2023 per arXiv; journal version Forum Math Pi 12 (2024) e22 (per search excerpt).
events.delivers: A reduction: the general Kronecker problem is equivalent to the same problem for reduced Kronecker coefficients. It gives no interpretation of any coefficient.
events.remains: The interpretation itself, now for reduced coefficients as well.
events.direction: Reduces the problem to reduced Kronecker coefficients rather than settling it; the two open questions now stand or fall together.

events.what_happened: Kyu-Hwan Lee, 'Machine-Learning Kronecker Coefficients', arXiv:2306.04734 (June 2023). Trains standard classifiers (nearest neighbours, convolutional networks, gradient-boosted trees) to predict whether a Kronecker coefficient is zero, at about 0.98 accuracy. This is not Soong Kyum Lee, author of the withdrawn three-row paper below.
events.delivers: An empirical vanishing predictor. No theorem and no interpretation.
events.direction: Predicts vanishing; does not bear on which way any interpretation cuts.

events.what_happened: Igor Pak and Greta Panova, 'Breaking down the reduced Kronecker coefficients', arXiv:2003.11398 (March 2020). Disproves the saturation property for reduced Kronecker coefficients and shows computing them is strongly #P-hard.
events.delivers: A counterexample to saturation for the reduced variant and a complexity result. Not an interpretation, and about the reduced coefficients rather than the Kronecker coefficients named in the bullet.
events.remains: The interpretation question for both families.
events.direction: Cuts against a simple saturation-based positive rule for the reduced variant. It is an analogue, not the bullet's question.

events.what_happened: Christian Ikenmeyer and Ravi Subramanian, 'Quantum complexity of the Kronecker coefficients', arXiv:2302.11454 (Feb 2023); published ACM Transactions on Quantum Computing (2025, doi 10.1145/3762673, per search excerpt). Shows computing Kronecker coefficients lies in #BQP.
events.revisions: Not checked beyond the journal reference in a search excerpt.
events.delivers: A quantum complexity upper bound for computing the coefficients. No interpretation.
events.direction: Complexity only; cuts neither way on interpretability.

events.what_happened: Giorgi Butbaia, Kyu-Hwan Lee and Fabian Ruehle, 'Interpretable Machine Learning for Kronecker Coefficients', arXiv:2502.11774 (first submitted 17 Feb 2025; listed cs.LG with math.CO, math.RT). Binary classifiers predict whether a Kronecker coefficient of S_n is zero. Interpretable models reach about 83% accuracy and give explicit decision formulas in terms of 'b-loadings'; transformer models reach over 99%.
events.revisions: v1 17 Feb 2025; ar5iv render dated March 2025 (per search excerpt); later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Empirical vanishing predictions and explicit decision formulas for a classifier. These are not a theorem about the coefficients and not an interpretation of them.
events.direction: Does not bear on which way an interpretation cuts. It is an empirical predictor of vanishing.

events.what_happened: Nate Harman and Alexander N. Wilson, 'Kronecker Coefficients, Crystals, and Bitableaux', arXiv:2507.14026 (submitted 18 July 2025; math.RT with math.CO cross-listing; 27 pages). Introduces bitableaux as candidate objects and states Conjecture 1 (per search excerpt of the paper): the Kronecker coefficients are counted by lexicographic bitableaux of given shape and weights satisfying a pair of Yamanouchi reading-word conditions. The authors say they have only a candidate procedure for extracting one of the reading words. They also obtain a combinatorial expansion of a Kronecker product of Schur functions in the monomial basis, which is a different basis from the Schur basis in the bullet. Related talks: Harman, SLMath workshop, 3 May 2024; Wilson, Fields Institute, 13 Feb 2026.
events.revisions: v1 18 July 2025 only, per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A conjectured interpretation for the Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients, with a candidate procedure for one reading word. Also an expansion for a monomial-basis Kronecker product of Schur functions, which is a different quantity. No proof of the conjecture is claimed.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, the second reading-word procedure, and a proof. Those are the parts of the bullet this result does not settle.
events.direction: Proposes a candidate interpretation of the Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients (a conjecture). Unproved, and it does not contradict the bullet.
events.object: Lexicographic bitableaux of given shape and weights, subject to a pair of Yamanouchi reading-word conditions. The authors conjecture these are counted by the Kronecker coefficient. The objects are not exhibited as a specific example. I did not read the definition of 'bitableau' because the PDF was unreadable; the description is from the abstract and search excerpt.

events.what_happened: Ernesto Vallejo and Pedro David Sanchez Salazar, 'On the computation of Kronecker coefficients I: column-row polytopes', arXiv:2510.16278 (v1 18 Oct 2025; v2 1 Jan 2026). Introduces column-row polytopes and gives several formulas for Kronecker coefficients as alternating sums of integer-point counts of these polytopes or their faces. The abstract refers to Kronecker coefficients in general. Comments say most results were presented at PRAM 2022 and VI CLAM 2021 talks, which predate the write-up. A 2011 talk by Sanchez Terraf described an earlier row-column polytope method for two-part third partitions (not checked in full).
events.revisions: v1 18 Oct 2025; v2 1 Jan 2026 (typos corrected, Theorem 6.5 added, per the comments field).
events.delivers: Formulas for Kronecker coefficients in general as alternating sums of lattice-point counts. Not a positive or manifestly nonnegative counting rule, and the authors do not claim one.
events.remains: A positive or manifestly nonnegative combinatorial interpretation; the title's 'Part I' suggests further parts, none found.
events.direction: A computational formula for all coefficients via alternating sums, which does not give the positive interpretation asked for. It cuts neither way on the existence of one.

events.what_happened: Igor Pak, Greta Panova and Joshua P. Swanson, 'A combinatorial interpretation for certain plethysm and Kronecker coefficients', arXiv:2511.02312 (v1 submitted 4 Nov 2025). Theorem 1.1 (v1 HTML): for lambda = (nk - r, r), g(lambda, (n^k), (n^k)) equals the number of marked KOH trees T(n, k, r). Theorem 1.2 gives plethysm coefficients for two-row lambda as counts of marked GOH trees. The authors state these are positive counts over explicit objects, and that the quantities are in FP, which is easier than the #P setting. Acknowledgements thank Gutierrez, Ikenmeyer and Orellana.
events.revisions: v1 4 Nov 2025; v2 8 Jun 2026; v3 27 Jul 2026. The v3 comment reads 'Minor corrections, final version. 13 pages. To appear in Proceedings of the AMS.' I read the v1 HTML and did not compare later versions.
events.delivers: A positive counting interpretation of the Kronecker coefficient g(lambda, (n^k), (n^k)) when lambda has two rows and both other partitions are rectangles (n^k). This is a restricted family: two-row first partition and two rectangular partitions. The paper says it does not claim a general interpretation.
events.remains: Every triple outside that family, including all triples with lambda of three or more rows and mu, nu not rectangular; the general interpretation asked for in the bullet.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the authors are established combinatorialists
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication, per the arXiv comment field. The acceptance was not verified with the journal.

events.directly_checkable: Small cases of g((nk-r, r), (n^k), (n^k)) can be computed by character calculations and compared with the tree counts. I did not run this check.
events.direction: Gives a positive interpretation for a restricted family of Kronecker coefficients. It moves the question for that family and leaves the general problem open.

events.what_happened: Soong Kyum Lee, 'Algebraic Obstructions and the Collapse of Elementary Structure in the Kronecker Problem', arXiv:2511.22856 (v1 28 Nov 2025; v2 2 Dec 2025; v3 20 Dec 2025 withdrawn). The versions claimed explicit closed forms for three-row Kronecker coefficients: g((n,n,1)^3) = 2 - (n mod 2) for n >= 3, five polynomial formulas for staircase-hook coefficients, and checks of Saxl's conjecture for five infinite families and 132 three-row partitions. The abstract reports a structural breakdown at parameter value 5. Authors' name differs from Kyu-Hwan Lee.
events.revisions: v1 28 Nov 2025; v2 2 Dec 2025; v3 20 Dec 2025, withdrawn. Mirrors disagree on the threshold (5 on the PDF, 55 in one HTML rendering) and on whether the Saxl check has a k <= 7 qualifier.
events.delivers: As claimed in v1-v2: closed forms for one family of three-row coefficients and polynomial formulas for staircase-hook coefficients. The withdrawal means these are not established by this record. The three-row restriction means the result is confined to a class of triples.
events.remains: All triples with three or more rows; the general interpretation asked for in the bullet.

checked_by.who: Unnamed expert reviewers, as reported by the author in the withdrawal comment
checked_by.what_they_did: Identified mathematical gaps in the paper, per the author's comment. The reviewers are not named and their reports are not public.

events.directly_checkable: The closed form g((n,n,1)^3) = 2 - (n mod 2) can be tested against character computations for small n. I did not run this check.
events.doubts: The author withdrew v3 (20 Dec 2025) with the comment: 'The claim of a complete proof is not justified in its current form' and 'This paper requires significant revision to address mathematical gaps identified by expert reviewers.' This is the author's own concession. The reviewers are not named.

withdrawn.what: Version 3 withdrawn by the author. The comment says the claim of a complete proof is not justified and that the paper needs significant revision to address gaps identified by expert reviewers.

events.direction: If it had stood, a closed form for a restricted (three-row) family, cutting toward explicit formulas there. Withdrawn, so the result is not established, and it does not reach the general problem either way.

events.what_happened: John M. Campbell, 'Kronecker coefficients via the Giambelli identity for Schur functions', arXiv:2604.23286 (submitted 25 Apr 2026; sole author; 48 pages; math.CO). Combines Littlewood's identity, the Giambelli identity for Schur functions, and Blasiak's colored Yamanouchi rule for hook shapes. Reduces the study of Kronecker coefficients to alternating sums over hook-indexed cases, and claims expansions of g(t, h1, h2) for two-row t and hook-like h1, h2 satisfying 'natural conditions', reduced 'in a cancellation-free manner' to new combinatorial formulas (per summarising fetch of the HTML).
events.revisions: v1 25 Apr 2026 only, per the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Combinatorial formulas for Kronecker coefficients g(t, h1, h2) where t is two-row and h1, h2 are hook-like under conditions I did not identify. This restricts the bullet to a family of triples. The general case is not covered.
events.remains: Triples in which t is not two-row, or h1 or h2 is not hook-like or fails the conditions; the general interpretation asked for in the bullet.
events.direction: Gives combinatorial formulas for a restricted family of triples, which cuts in favour of an interpretation existing there. It leaves the general problem open.

events.what_happened: Josaphat Baolahy and Benjamin Randrianirina, 'Species, Symmetric Functions, and Kronecker Product', arXiv:2604.10336 (v1 11 Apr 2026; math.CO). Constructs two new bases of the homogeneous symmetric functions of degree n from species, shows the species are closed under the Kronecker (Hadamard) product with nonnegative integer structure constants, and says this suggests routes toward interpreting those constants. It poses Question 5.1 of the later paper, which answers it. Published in Enumerative Combinatorics and Applications 6:3 (2026) per search excerpt, not opened.
events.delivers: Species-basis structure constants are nonnegative and the species are closed under the Kronecker product. No formula for the Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet: the Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients are not addressed.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published (per search excerpt; the journal page was not opened)

events.direction: Concerns a different basis (species, not Schur). It cuts neither way on the Schur-basis problem.

events.what_happened: Josaphat Baolahy and Benjamin Randrianirina, 'The Molecular Species C_alpha: Geometric Realization and a Closed Formula for Kronecker Coefficients', arXiv:2609.05010 (v1 4 Sep 2026; v2 10 Sep 2026; math.CO). Realises the species C_alpha as periodic patterns and gives Theorem 4.1, a closed formula for the species coefficients b^lambda_{alpha,beta} in C_alpha x C_beta = sum over lambda of b^lambda_{alpha,beta} C_lambda, using o(sigma_alpha), o(sigma_beta), gcd, Mobius and Euler totient. The introduction says this answers Question 5.1 of arXiv:2604.10336. The paper says the positive combinatorial rule for the classical Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients g remains one of the most important open problems in algebraic combinatorics (Stanley), and it does not claim one for g.
events.revisions: v1 4 Sep 2026; v2 10 Sep 2026. I read the v2 HTML; I did not compare the versions.
events.delivers: A closed formula for the species-basis coefficients b^lambda_{alpha,beta}, a different quantity from the Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients g(lambda, mu, nu). The title calls it a closed formula for Kronecker coefficients, but the body says the classical problem remains open and b is the species counterpart of the Garsia-Remmel constants.
events.remains: The Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients, which is what the bullet asks about. Nothing in the paper gives an interpretation of them.
events.directly_checkable: The numerical consistency checks were run in SageMath (computer algebra), not in a proof assistant. I did not run them.
events.doubts: Scope: the title says 'Closed Formula for Kronecker Coefficients' but the closed formula is for b^lambda_{alpha,beta}, which the paper distinguishes from the classical g. A reader using titles would count an event that the body disclaims.
events.direction: Gives a closed formula for a related species-basis quantity. It cuts neither way on the Schur-basis question, which the paper says remains open.

systems.name: Anthropic's Claude
systems.what_it_did: The authors say Claude was used 'as an AI assistant for exploration and proof verification' and 'to polish the English grammar and stylistic flow of the manuscript'. They say they 'rigorously reviewed all AI-generated and computational output'. The sentences do not say which mathematical statement, if any, Claude produced. Whether its role is load-bearing is not settled by the text: 'exploration' may or may not have supplied mathematics that is in Theorem 4.1, and 'proof verification' may mean checking only.
systems.basis_quote: Additionally, the authors acknowledge the use of Anthropic's Claude as an AI assistant for exploration and proof verification ... The authors rigorously reviewed all AI-generated and computational output and assume full responsibility for the final mathematical results and text.

summary: Searches (37 WebSearch calls, plus opened pages) found no event that gives a combinatorial interpretation of the Schur-basis Kronecker coefficients for all triples, and none that changes Stanley's Problem 10 from open. In-window events: (1) Harman and Wilson (arXiv 2507.14026, 18 Jul 2025) conjecture that the coefficients count lexicographic bitableaux with Yamanouchi reading-word conditions. They report only partial results, in a different basis; the PDF was unreadable to me, so the conjecture statement comes from a search excerpt. (2) Vallejo and Sanchez Salazar (arXiv 2510.16278, 18 Oct 2025) compute all coefficients by alternating lattice-point sums. That is computable but not a positive interpretation, and I count it as not one. (3) Pak, Panova and Swanson (arXiv 2511.02312, 4 Nov 2025) give positive tree-counts for g(lambda, (n^k), (n^k)) with lambda two-row. This is a real, restricted interpretation (I read the v1 HTML; the arXiv comment reports acceptance by PAMS, unverified). (4) Lee (arXiv 2511.22856, 28 Nov 2025) claimed closed forms for three-row coefficients; the author withdrew v3 on 20 Dec 2025, saying the claim of a complete proof is not justified and that expert reviewers found gaps. The reviewers are unnamed. Lee is not Kyu-Hwan Lee, who wrote the machine-learning papers. (5) Campbell (arXiv 2604.23286, 25 Apr 2026) gives combinatorial formulas for g(t, h1, h2) with t two-row and h1, h2 hook-like under conditions I could not identify from the readable text. This is a restricted family; the 'cancellation-free' step is the authors' claim as I read it from a summary. (6) Baolahy and Randrianirina (arXiv 2609.05010, 4 Sep 2026) give a closed formula for species-basis coefficients b, which their title calls 'Kronecker coefficients'. Their introduction says the classical problem remains open, so I record it as a different question. The paper's acknowledgements name Anthropic's Claude. Close calls. (a) Whether Campbell's families count as moving the problem. Both readings: the families are infinite and are genuine interpretations, but the bullet asks for all triples. (b) Whether the Baolahy-Randrianirina title's 'closed formula for Kronecker coefficients' should count. The body disclaims it. (c) Whether Claude's role in Baolahy-Randrianirina is load-bearing. I placed it in ai.systems because 'AI-generated ... output' is ambiguous and the authors do not say which parts. The only other AI disclosure is Campbell's acknowledgement (Section 6): 'The author used the GPT-5.3 model to assist with the exposition and with exploratory calculations and to explore heuristic arguments, but all mathematical proofs, results, exposition, etc. were/was written by the author and verified independently by the author.' I left GPT-5.3 out of ai.systems because the author says the proofs are their own; it is named in the summary for the later pass. The Campbell quote came from a summarising fetch of the HTML, not raw text, because the PDF was unreadable. Pre-window background: Blasiak (2012) gives a positive rule for hook shapes; Ballantine and Orellana (2005) for two-row first partition outside a square; Ikenmeyer and Panova (arXiv 4 May 2023, Forum Math Pi 2024) reduce the problem to reduced Kronecker coefficients, so Stanley's Problem 10 and Kirillov's 2.32 are equivalent; Ikenmeyer, Mulmuley and Walter (2015) show positivity is NP-hard. Wikipedia's 'Kronecker coefficient' article (opened; last edited 17 June 2026 per the summary) still presents the combinatorial description as unsolved and mentions no 2024-2026 development. Nothing in the searches linked any AI system to a result on the classical problem. The AlphaEvolve paper (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao, Wagner, arXiv 2511.02864, 3 Nov 2025) has an abstract that does not mention Kronecker coefficients; its 81-page body was not read. OpenAI's 2026 announcements (unit-distance, 'Astra') appeared in search results with no Kronecker mention in the snippets; I did not open them. Machine-learning predictors of vanishing (Lee 2023; Butbaia, Lee, Ruehle 2025) are AI involvement of a kind, but they make no theorem about the coefficients, and I record no named system for them.
competing_reading: Read the bullet as asking for an interpretation of a useful family, and the window moved: Pak, Panova and Swanson (positive tree counts for rectangular-two-row triples) and Campbell (formulas for two-row/hook-like triples) are real interpretations, and Harman and Wilson give a candidate for everything. Read it strictly as all triples and no result in the window moves it. A reader who reads titles would count Baolahy and Randrianirina as a Kronecker result, which the paper's body does not support.
what_would_settle_it: For the general problem: a proof or disproof of Harman and Wilson's conjecture, or any positive rule for arbitrary triples. For Campbell: the 'natural conditions' on h1 and h2, and whether the 'cancellation-free' reduction holds, checked by a referee. For Baolahy and Randrianirina: whether Theorem 4.1 says anything about classical g, the v1-v2 differences, and a fuller account of what Claude did in the proof. For Lee: the reviewers' reports or a corrected version. For Pak, Panova and Swanson: the PAMS acceptance and the v3 text. For the AI question: the full texts of Harman and Wilson and of Vallejo and Sanchez Salazar, since neither was readable to me.
